title: §27-003: Service Meshes, API Gateways & Serialization Efficiency
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §27-003 (Service Meshes, API Gateways & Serialization Efficiency).

cards.concept: Service Meshes, API Gateways & Serialization Efficiency: gRPC & Protocol Buffers Efficiency
cards.question: Why does gRPC over HTTP/2 deliver significantly higher throughput and lower latency than traditional REST over JSON?

options.text: gRPC compiles JavaScript into native assembly at runtime.
Protocol Buffers uses compact binary serialization (varints, field tags) eliminating JSON text parsing overhead, and HTTP/2 multiplexes concurrent RPCs over a single persistent TCP connection.
gRPC operates exclusively over UDP without handshakes.
REST requires manual encryption of each HTTP header.

cards.explanation: Protobuf encodes structured data into binary format without field name string overhead. HTTP/2 multiplexing prevents head-of-line blocking and reuses connections efficiently.
cards.pitfall: Altering existing Protocol Buffer field tag numbers breaks backward and forward compatibility across microservice versions.
cards.citation: gRPC Official Documentation: Core Concepts / Protocol Buffers Encoding

cards.concept: Service Meshes, API Gateways & Serialization Efficiency: Protocol Buffer Schema Evolution Rules
cards.question: When updating a `.proto` service definition in production, what rule MUST be strictly followed to preserve backward and forward compatibility?

options.text: Field names cannot be longer than 8 characters.
Never change the numeric tag identifier of an existing field; if removing a field, mark its tag as `reserved` to prevent reuse.
All fields must be marked required in proto3.
Proto files must be recompiled simultaneously across all microservices.

cards.explanation: Protobuf serializes field tags, not field names. Changing a field tag corrupts data decoding in older services. Removed tags must be marked 'reserved' so future fields don't accidentally reuse them.
cards.pitfall: Reusing a deleted tag number for a new field causes older microservices to decode new data into old field types, causing silent data corruption.
cards.citation: Protocol Buffers Documentation: Updating A Message Type
